responseOptions.playerText: Laughing at the wrong moment and admitting it.
responseOptions.suspectReply: That is excellent. A polished person makes me wonder where they store the inconvenient parts.

responseOptions.playerText: Getting excited enough to forget what they were saying.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Yes. Enthusiasm should be allowed to ruin a sentence occasionally.

stages.suspectMessage: Once a municipal tree report is signed, even I cannot edit it. The city preserves every dull version forever, which is annoying until someone insists you changed your mind later. Do you keep old drafts?

responseOptions.playerText: Only the embarrassing ones, apparently.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Naturally. The useful versions vanish while the awkward ones achieve immortality.

responseOptions.playerText: No, I enjoy rewriting what past me was thinking.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Very healthy. Past me receives far less mercy, especially when she approved an ugly spreadsheet.

stages.suspectMessage: I balanced a community budget to the cent and then bought three pastries because choosing one felt emotionally irresponsible. Are you sensible with small pleasures?

responseOptions.playerText: I budget for being a little unreasonable.
responseOptions.suspectReply: That may be the most responsible answer possible. Joy deserves its own category.

responseOptions.playerText: No. Bakeries make all my principles negotiable.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Good. I distrust anyone who can remain financially disciplined near warm bread.

stages.suspectMessage: My work is deciding which useful thing gets funded first. I hate pretending numbers make the human part disappear. What would you protect from a tight budget?

responseOptions.playerText: Anything that gives people somewhere to belong.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Exactly. A shared room can look optional on paper and become essential in real life.

responseOptions.playerText: Good food. People solve more problems after eating.
responseOptions.suspectReply: A defensible policy. Hungry committees have approved some terrible ideas.

stages.suspectMessage: Equipment invoices repeat automatically once the annual budget is signed. Months later they arrive in my inbox like very boring prophecies. What recurring task always surprises you?

responseOptions.playerText: Changing the bedsheets. Time moves differently around that job.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Yes. Fresh sheets are wonderful, but the process returns with suspicious speed.

responseOptions.playerText: Buying toothpaste. I never remember finishing the previous one.
responseOptions.suspectReply: The empty tube appears without any believable history. A small domestic mystery.

stages.suspectMessage: I recorded rain for work today and accidentally captured two pigeons having what sounded like a serious disagreement. What ordinary sound do you enjoy?

responseOptions.playerText: Someone cooking in the next room.
responseOptions.suspectReply: That is a good one. You hear care happening before you see it.

responseOptions.playerText: A train passing when I am already home.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Perfect. Movement is much more relaxing when it does not require you to pack.

stages.suspectMessage: Radio has made me comfortable with silence. A pause can mean someone is thinking, not that the conversation needs emergency repair. How do you handle an awkward quiet moment?

responseOptions.playerText: I let it exist for a while.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Excellent. Most silences become harmless if nobody starts fighting them.

responseOptions.playerText: I ask a question that is probably too specific.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Also effective. Specific questions are how strangers suddenly become interesting.

stages.suspectMessage: For outdoor pieces I leave a weather recorder overnight on an automatic timer, then collect it after breakfast. It hears far more nightlife than I do. What would a recorder outside your window capture?

responseOptions.playerText: Bicycles, one loud neighbor, and me closing the window.
responseOptions.suspectReply: A complete urban composition with a strong final movement.

responseOptions.playerText: Mostly birds and an embarrassingly early delivery truck.
responseOptions.suspectReply: That sounds peaceful until the truck arrives as percussion.

stages.suspectMessage: I drew the same leaf for three hours and discovered it had been upside down the entire time. Please tell me your day contained a more dignified achievement.

responseOptions.playerText: I remembered an appointment before the reminder.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Exceptional. You have earned the right to feel superior to both me and the leaf.

responseOptions.playerText: I made dinner without creating every dirty dish I own.
responseOptions.suspectReply: That is advanced domestic technique. I usually achieve food or dignity, never both.

stages.suspectMessage: Drawing plants teaches you that precision and beauty are not the same thing. The accurate leaf is often the stranger one. Do you prefer neatness or character?

responseOptions.playerText: Character, provided I am not the person cleaning afterward.
responseOptions.suspectReply: A reasonable boundary. I support charming disorder from a safe distance.

responseOptions.playerText: Neatness at home, character everywhere else.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Very wise. Let the world be interesting while the kitchen remains findable.

stages.suspectMessage: I sometimes photograph saplings after sunset at the nursery because the leaves finally stop moving. My camera roll looks mysterious until you notice every dramatic shadow contains a plant label. What makes your photos look stranger than your life?

responseOptions.playerText: I photograph signs with accidental spelling mistakes.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Then your camera roll is a quiet archive of public embarrassment. I approve.

responseOptions.playerText: Close-ups of things I want to remember how to repair.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Practical and oddly intimate. A broken hinge can become a family portrait.

stages.suspectMessage: I found a watering-system failure today that turned out to be one loose wire. Three people had already blamed the weather, the software, and possibly fate. Are you good at starting with the simple answer?

responseOptions.playerText: Only after trying two unnecessarily complicated ones.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Honest. Complexity is very flattering until the loose wire laughs at you.

responseOptions.playerText: Usually, but I still enjoy a dramatic theory.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Same. I keep the dramatic theory for entertainment and check the plug first.

stages.suspectMessage: I like practical work because a pipe does not pretend to be fine out of politeness. People are harder. What helps you say something is wrong?

responseOptions.playerText: Knowing the other person will not punish the honesty.
responseOptions.suspectReply: That is everything. Safety makes directness possible.

responseOptions.playerText: Saying it early, before I build a speech around it.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Excellent strategy. My worst conversations begin after three rehearsals in the shower.

stages.suspectMessage: A pressure test means switching soil sensors off overnight so wet ground does not complain to the system every six minutes. What part of your work sounds suspicious without context?

responseOptions.playerText: Deleting old files until the important folder looks empty.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Yes, context is doing heroic work there.

responseOptions.playerText: Keeping notes about mistakes people make repeatedly.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Useful, sensible, and absolutely terrible when described at a party.

stages.suspectMessage: I sent twelve trees onto motorways today, which sounds more magical than checking straps and delivery numbers. What part of your job deserves a better description?

responseOptions.playerText: Answering emails could become managing distant expectations.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Beautiful. I may borrow that when somebody asks why I look tired.

responseOptions.playerText: Meetings could become organized uncertainty.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Accurate and generous. Most meetings never become organized.

stages.suspectMessage: Dispatch work made me appreciate people who say they are running late before they are already late. Which tiny act makes someone trustworthy to you?

responseOptions.playerText: Doing the small thing they said they would do.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Exactly. Reliability is built from terribly uncinematic moments.

responseOptions.playerText: Admitting they forgot instead of inventing a story.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Yes. A plain mistake is much easier to forgive than an elaborate performance.

stages.suspectMessage: I photograph both sides of every brass nursery marker before loading. One mislabeled maple taught me that a boring picture can save a week of arguing. What dull habit has rescued you?

responseOptions.playerText: Putting appointments in my calendar immediately.
responseOptions.suspectReply: A heroic habit. Future you should send present you flowers.

responseOptions.playerText: Keeping spare keys with someone reliable.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Also excellent, provided reliable does not mean someone who lives two hours away.

stages.suspectMessage: I spent this afternoon helping someone choose between three nearly identical cardigans because only one felt like hers. What small thing makes you feel most like yourself?

responseOptions.playerText: Music playing while I make breakfast.
responseOptions.suspectReply: I understand that. The right song can put a familiar shape around the whole morning.

responseOptions.playerText: Walking without deciding the route first.
responseOptions.suspectReply: That sounds freeing. A little uncertainty feels different when nobody is rushing you.

stages.suspectMessage: I volunteer with trees because care is wonderfully uncomplicated there. Water, patience, shelter when the frost comes. People rarely tell you what they need so clearly. What do you find easy to care about?

responseOptions.playerText: Animals. They make honesty look effortless.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Yes. My dog has never hidden disappointment, especially when dinner is late.

responseOptions.playerText: Places people share without needing permission to stay.
responseOptions.suspectReply: I like that. Belonging feels most real when nobody is checking whether you earned the chair.

stages.suspectMessage: Can I ask you a dangerously domestic question? Forget rent, commuting, and all the furniture we pretend we could assemble. What would make a future home feel unmistakably yours?

responseOptions.playerText: A noisy kitchen, friends letting themselves in, and a garden that never quite behaves.
responseOptions.suspectReply: That is almost unfairly lovely. I can already picture someone stealing food from the pan while the dog brings half the garden inside. I envy how easily you said it. Mine always has Sunday noise spilling out of the kitchen, an apple tree producing more than we can eat, a blue front door, muddy paw prints in the hall, and no boxes waiting for the next move. Somewhere permanent enough to grow old.

responseOptions.playerText: A small place near water, big windows, too many books, and someone who makes leaving unnecessary.
responseOptions.suspectReply: That sounds like the kind of place where your shoulders drop the moment you walk through the door. I envy that certainty. Mine always has Sunday noise spilling out of the kitchen, an apple tree producing more than we can eat, a blue front door, muddy paw prints in the hall, and no boxes waiting for the next move. Somewhere permanent enough to grow old.

stages.suspectMessage: I photographed a birthday today where the best picture happened after the cake leaned sideways and everyone tried to save it at once. What moment would you rather remember than pose?

responseOptions.playerText: The laugh after someone ruins the serious photograph.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Always better. Relief makes people look more like themselves.

responseOptions.playerText: The quiet five minutes after everyone leaves.
responseOptions.suspectReply: I love that answer. Empty rooms keep a little warmth for a while.

stages.suspectMessage: People become tense when a camera appears, so I usually start by admitting I dislike being photographed too. What makes you forget to be self-conscious?

responseOptions.playerText: Being genuinely interested in what someone is saying.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Exactly. Attention is wonderfully incompatible with posing.

responseOptions.playerText: Doing something with my hands.
responseOptions.suspectReply: That works beautifully. Give someone a task and their real face comes back.

stages.suspectMessage: For early volunteer shoots I take the first train and begin photographing on the walk from the station. By the time everyone is posing, I already have bicycles, coffee cups, and terrible morning hair. What would your honest morning photograph show?

responseOptions.playerText: One open eye and unreasonable loyalty to a coffee mug.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Perfect. I would keep the mug sharp and let dignity remain softly out of focus.

responseOptions.playerText: Me negotiating with an alarm I personally set.
responseOptions.suspectReply: A timeless portrait of betrayal between a person and yesterday's optimism.

stages.suspectMessage: I spent lunch watching people ignore the paved path and create a better one through the grass. Do you follow the intended route when nobody is watching?

responseOptions.playerText: Only if it is actually the best route.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Good. Design should earn obedience rather than demand it.

responseOptions.playerText: Usually. I worry the shortcut exists for a bad reason.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Also sensible. Some mysterious paths end at fences and regret.

stages.suspectMessage: My favorite places are useful without feeling controlling. A bench can suggest rest without ordering anyone to sit. What place makes you linger?

responseOptions.playerText: A courtyard hidden behind a busy street.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Yes. Finding quiet near noise makes both feel more interesting.

responseOptions.playerText: Anywhere with water and somewhere comfortable to sit.
responseOptions.suspectReply: A reliable combination. Moving water does most of the conversational work.

stages.suspectMessage: Tree locations are committee decisions, even when one planner's name appears on the final map. Twelve people can debate a patch of shade for weeks. What harmless decision takes you far too long?

responseOptions.playerText: Choosing where to eat when everyone says anything is fine.
responseOptions.suspectReply: That phrase has ended more peaceful evenings than actual disagreement.

responseOptions.playerText: Buying a lamp. Apparently every room has a lighting philosophy.
responseOptions.suspectReply: It does, and the wrong lamp will remind you nightly that you compromised.

stages.suspectMessage: One of my students apologized to a basil plant today. The plant probably deserved it, but I admired the accountability. What are you happily bad at?

responseOptions.playerText: Singing, especially when I know all the words.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Excellent. Accuracy would only distract from commitment.

responseOptions.playerText: Keeping herbs alive, apparently.
responseOptions.suspectReply: I offer a judgment-free consultation, though the basil may have its own opinion.

stages.suspectMessage: Teaching adults is mostly convincing people that one mistake did not reveal their true inability to grow anything. What makes learning easier for you?

responseOptions.playerText: Someone explaining why, not only what.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Exactly. Instructions become much kinder when they include a reason.

responseOptions.playerText: Being allowed to fail without an audience.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Very fair. Confidence grows better without spectators leaning over it.

stages.suspectMessage: On planting mornings, instructors arrive after contractors uncover and level the prepared pits. We inherit the tidy part and look far more capable than we deserve. Which finished result hides the most chaos in your life?

responseOptions.playerText: Dinner for friends. They never see the kitchen ten minutes earlier.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Hospitality is partly the art of closing the correct door.

responseOptions.playerText: Any message that sounds calm. The first draft usually has weather.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Relatable. Composure is often just panic after editing.

stages.suspectMessage: I rejected the headline 'Scandal You Won't Believe' this afternoon, so I have already improved civilization a little. How was your day?

responseOptions.playerText: Less heroic. I answered emails and successfully remembered lunch.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Remembering lunch puts you ahead of most newsrooms. I once ate almonds from a coat pocket and called it a meal.

responseOptions.playerText: I also prevented a disaster, but only because I caught the wrong train.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Accidental competence is still competence. Please save the full train story for a drink.

stages.suspectMessage: My small luxury is a long breakfast with an actual newspaper and nowhere to be. What ordinary thing makes your week better?

responseOptions.playerText: Fresh bread while it is still warm enough to ruin the butter.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Excellent answer. I know a bakery with no chairs, so we would have to walk and pretend the crumbs do not prove our impatience.

responseOptions.playerText: An evening when nobody checks the time first.
responseOptions.suspectReply: That is rarer than fresh bread. I like conversations that quietly outlive the plan made for them.

stages.suspectMessage: A line my editor hears too often is this: if a documented truth ruins a powerful man's reputation, the lie caused the damage. Too severe for a dating profile?

responseOptions.playerText: Severe, but honest. What are you like when you are not working?
responseOptions.suspectReply: Softer, slower, and much too invested in secondhand bookshops. I do not cross-examine anyone before coffee.

responseOptions.playerText: Only if every conversation becomes a headline.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Fair warning accepted. On a date I would rather learn your worst travel snack than your public position on anything.

stages.suspectMessage: I left court with a perfectly prepared dinner plan and somehow ended up making noodles at half past ten. Are you loyal to plans or to hunger?

responseOptions.playerText: Hunger. A plan that ignores it has already failed.
responseOptions.suspectReply: A persuasive opening argument. I would add chili oil and withdraw every objection.

responseOptions.playerText: Plans, until somebody suggests noodles convincingly.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Then I need only prepare a convincing noodle proposal. Finally, a manageable workload.

stages.suspectMessage: My harmless strong opinion is that dessert should be ordered before everyone starts lying about being full. What is yours?

responseOptions.playerText: Window seats belong to whoever actually looks out of the window.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Reasonable and enforceable. I would happily surrender it if you promise commentary on passing dogs.

responseOptions.playerText: Music sounds better when nobody can skip after twenty seconds.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Agreed. A song deserves enough time to make its case, even if it loses.

stages.suspectMessage: Work has made me impatient with one thing: some men treat a dismissed charge like a certificate of innocence. Escaping punishment proves that a case failed. It proves nothing else.

responseOptions.playerText: That sounds exhausting to carry home every night.
responseOptions.suspectReply: It can be. That is why home contains loud records, soft clothes, and absolutely no legal television.

responseOptions.playerText: Can you still leave room for people to surprise you?
responseOptions.suspectReply: I have to. Certainty is useful in a filing and dangerous in a person. Surprise me over noodles.

stages.suspectMessage: I coordinate security for public events and locked myself out of my own flat yesterday. You may enjoy that irony for free.

responseOptions.playerText: Only if you tell me how long you pretended it was intentional.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Twelve minutes. Then my neighbor found me eating emergency mints on the stairs and ended the performance.

responseOptions.playerText: I respect a professional who creates her own practical exam.
responseOptions.suspectReply: I passed eventually, but the locksmith's feedback lacked warmth.

stages.suspectMessage: I automatically notice exits, loose cables, and anyone arguing with a door. What habit from your work follows you into real life?

responseOptions.playerText: I rewrite badly worded menus in my head.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Useful. You repair the menu, I confirm the emergency exit, and eventually we remember to order.

responseOptions.playerText: I estimate how long every simple task will take and remain wrong.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Perfect. I build schedules, then watch important people ignore them with extraordinary confidence.

stages.suspectMessage: Security is mostly noticing the person who expects every rule to move for him. They are usually surprised when a locked door stays locked.

responseOptions.playerText: Do you enjoy being the person who says no?
responseOptions.suspectReply: Only when it keeps everyone safe. Off duty I am easily persuaded by street food and terrible escape rooms.

responseOptions.playerText: I imagine that gives you a good sense of character.
responseOptions.suspectReply: A partial one. The real test is how somebody treats the cleaner after the important guests leave.

stages.suspectMessage: Chairman Meow has occupied my clean laundry and rejected my appeal. Do you live with an animal, a plant, or complete domestic freedom?

responseOptions.playerText: A plant that survives mostly to prove me wrong.
responseOptions.suspectReply: An adversarial but stable relationship. Chairman prefers emotional manipulation and direct control of all blankets.

responseOptions.playerText: Complete freedom, although the laundry still makes demands.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Laundry is less affectionate but equally confident that your time belongs to it.

stages.suspectMessage: What restores your faith in people after a bad week? Mine is someone helping quietly and leaving before the thank-you speech.

responseOptions.playerText: A stranger being patient when impatience would be easier.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Yes. Decency is most convincing when nobody thinks it will be remembered.

responseOptions.playerText: Friends who arrive with food instead of advice.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Those are the friends to keep. Advice cools badly; soup usually survives the journey.

stages.suspectMessage: My work changed one instinct in me. I stopped believing every powerful man deserves advance warning. Sometimes a family needs to file first and explain later.

responseOptions.playerText: That sounds less harsh with the second sentence.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Context saves me often. My angry face arrives before my careful explanation and refuses to wait outside.

responseOptions.playerText: Does it make it hard to trust new people?
responseOptions.suspectReply: Harder, not impossible. Trust should be offered in small honest pieces, preferably while sharing chocolate.

stages.suspectMessage: I promise I do not score dates in spreadsheets. I did once make a chart proving my friends always cancel plans when it rains, but that was public service.

responseOptions.playerText: Did the chart change their behavior?
responseOptions.suspectReply: No, but it made the cancellations statistically satisfying. I still brought pastries and forgave everyone.

responseOptions.playerText: How many data points before friendship becomes surveillance?
responseOptions.suspectReply: At least twelve. Fewer than that is affectionate observation with colored labels.

stages.suspectMessage: Which prediction are you happiest to get wrong? I always predict that I will leave parties early and then order another plate for the table.

responseOptions.playerText: That a quiet evening will be boring.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Good company destroys that forecast beautifully. Quiet is only empty when nobody is curious.

responseOptions.playerText: That I already know what kind of person I will like.
responseOptions.suspectReply: My favorite result is the one that makes the original theory look embarrassingly confident.

stages.suspectMessage: With the right spreadsheet, I can end a career before lunch. To be clear, I mean a terrible polling forecast, not a supervillain plan.

responseOptions.playerText: The clarification arrived suspiciously quickly.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Occupational hazard. Numbers sound sinister when politicians discover they are unpopular.

responseOptions.playerText: Can a chart ever make you feel sorry for someone?
responseOptions.suspectReply: Often. A falling line is still made of people having difficult days. That part should never become abstract.

stages.suspectMessage: A market vendor gave me free coffee because I remembered his birthday. This is the only political influence I intend to brag about today.

responseOptions.playerText: Remembering birthdays is a respectable campaign strategy.
responseOptions.suspectReply: It wins coffee and occasional cake. My actual campaign team should take notes.

responseOptions.playerText: I would vote for anyone promising reliable coffee.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Dangerous. I also promise a karaoke performance you will immediately regret supporting.

stages.suspectMessage: Choose carefully: an excellent singer who refuses duets, or a terrible singer who commits completely?

responseOptions.playerText: The terrible singer. Courage deserves company.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Correct. Enthusiasm can carry a chorus much farther than dignity.

responseOptions.playerText: The excellent singer, if I am allowed to handle applause.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Practical, but I will eventually drag you into the final verse. Public participation is important.

stages.suspectMessage: Give me the right document and I can end a career before breakfast. It sounds brutal, but public office should survive the truth.

responseOptions.playerText: Do you ever worry that you enjoy the fight too much?
responseOptions.suspectReply: Absolutely. That is why I keep people around who tell me when principle has started enjoying the microphone.

responseOptions.playerText: And what should survive a first date?
responseOptions.suspectReply: Two honest opinions, one shared dessert, and ideally no campaign promises at all.

stages.suspectMessage: I escaped a reception with two bread rolls in my handbag. Please tell me your evening has better standards.

responseOptions.playerText: I ate dinner over the sink, so we are operating at similar levels.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Then neither of us may judge the other. Mine at least came with a speech about regional investment.

responseOptions.playerText: My standards are excellent. My dinner was cereal, but the bowl was clean.
responseOptions.suspectReply: A clean bowl transforms everything. I would have added one stolen bread roll and called it a tasting menu.

stages.suspectMessage: Public life makes everyone ask about ambitions. My private answer is a sofa dinner, phones face down, and nowhere else we are expected. What ordinary evening feels luxurious to you?

responseOptions.playerText: Cooking together slowly, even if dinner turns out badly.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Perfect. I bring confidence unsupported by skill, so patience and emergency bread would both be useful.

responseOptions.playerText: A long walk followed by choosing dessert before dinner.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Decisive and slightly rebellious. I spend all day negotiating; dessert should require no coalition.

stages.suspectMessage: What makes you lose respect for someone, even when everyone else finds him impressive?

responseOptions.playerText: Hurting people, then using charm to make the consequences disappear.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Exactly. I have met enough polished men to know that a clean suit is not the same as clean hands. Sorry, that sounded like a speech. I promise to be less dramatic over coffee.

responseOptions.playerText: Refusing responsibility while expecting everyone else to admire the performance.
responseOptions.suspectReply: That is mine too. I have met enough polished men to know that a clean suit is not the same as clean hands. You may interrupt me if our first coffee becomes a press conference.

stages.suspectMessage: I served dinner to two hundred guests today and am now overthinking what I would cook for one interesting person. Does toast count as confidence or surrender?

responseOptions.playerText: Confidence, if the toppings have ambition.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Excellent. I have tomatoes, soft cheese, and professional access to herbs that deserve a better evening than mine.

responseOptions.playerText: Surrender can be romantic if nobody pretends otherwise.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Then toast, good butter, and honesty. That may be a stronger menu than half the receptions I cater.

stages.suspectMessage: How do you know a dinner went well? My test is that someone starts clearing plates, everyone stops them, and another hour disappears.

responseOptions.playerText: When the chairs become uncomfortable before the conversation does.
responseOptions.suspectReply: That is beautifully accurate. I own several attractive chairs that fail this test within forty minutes.

responseOptions.playerText: When nobody remembers who suggested leaving first.
responseOptions.suspectReply: The ideal ending. My work runs by the minute, so losing track of one feels wonderfully irresponsible.

stages.suspectMessage: For formal guests, privacy begins with a closed door and a table nobody interrupts. That sounds sinister when typed by a caterer. I only mean people relax when nobody photographs their soup.

responseOptions.playerText: What would make you relax at our table?
responseOptions.suspectReply: Shared plates, no schedule, and knowing you will laugh kindly if I spill something first.

responseOptions.playerText: Now I need to know which soup deserves secrecy.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Anything pale under overhead lighting. Some reputations really can be saved by closing a door.

stages.suspectMessage: I spent the afternoon repairing a century-old letter and the evening apologizing to a houseplant I forgot to water. Which one sounds more like me?

responseOptions.playerText: The apology. The letter cannot judge you from the windowsill.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Correct. The fern has a dramatic posture and knows exactly how to use it.

responseOptions.playerText: The letter. You remembered every crease but forgot the watering can.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Also correct. Apparently I am best with objects whose needs stopped changing decades ago.

stages.suspectMessage: What have you kept for no practical reason? Mine is a tram ticket from the day my sister and I got lost and found our favorite cafe.

responseOptions.playerText: A receipt with a joke written on the back.
responseOptions.suspectReply: That is exactly the sort of document archives reject and people actually need.

responseOptions.playerText: A key that no longer opens anything I own.
responseOptions.suspectReply: I understand that completely. Some objects keep belonging after their practical purpose ends.

stages.suspectMessage: My least charming professional belief is that buried records always return when somebody remembers where to look. Paper is much more patient than people expect.

responseOptions.playerText: That sounds comforting and threatening at the same time.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Archivists hear that often. I am personally much less threatening and much easier to distract with cake.

responseOptions.playerText: What would you want someone to remember about you?
responseOptions.suspectReply: That quiet did not mean absent. Also that I always knew the museum cafe with the shortest queue.

stages.suspectMessage: My dachshund walked away during my best impression, which is the clearest review I received all week. What reliably makes you laugh?

responseOptions.playerText: Someone committing fully to a joke that is already failing.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Excellent. Courage without quality is the foundation of half my voice impressions.

responseOptions.playerText: Animals interrupting people who think they are important.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Then Otto is a professional satirist. His timing is excellent and his fee is cheese.

stages.suspectMessage: I think a personal apology is the one subject never improved by a microphone. If it needs applause, something has gone wrong. What should stay private?

responseOptions.playerText: The first honest conversation after an argument.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Yes. No audience, no scorekeeping, and no clever closing line saved for later.

responseOptions.playerText: Any kindness that becomes advertising when filmed.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Exactly. A camera can turn generosity into a person congratulating herself in high definition.

stages.suspectMessage: My most unpopular line is that public shame can be a civic service when private apologies are only performances. The audience usually laughs, then realizes I am serious.

responseOptions.playerText: Do you ever regret making someone the joke?
responseOptions.suspectReply: Yes, and I should. Power deserves scrutiny, but a person should never become invisible behind the punchline.

responseOptions.playerText: Can you switch that part of your brain off on a date?
responseOptions.suspectReply: Mostly. If you say something ridiculous I may remember it forever, but I promise not to sell tickets.
